solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Group organised by wife to become more adult

indicators.note: letters that are organised are put into a new order, so the word group is rearranged

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A collection of people, arranged with the help of someone's wife, sets out to mature.
explanation.walkthrough: UPGROW is a rare, old-fashioned verb; 'to' is a link that marks the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To upgrow is an old verb meaning to grow up, that is, to mature into an adult.

clue.text: Quiet snoring sound stifling a flamboyant quality

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: the snore stifles the a by smothering it, holding it inside

parts.note: zzz is the cartoon sound of someone snoring

explanation.surface: A soft snore smothers any hint of showiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stifling' puts A inside ZZZ, making ZAZZ after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pzazz, also pizzazz, is flair and vitality, an attractive showy energy.

clue.text: British rule in shock after uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry an uprising reads upward, so the word for shock is read backwards

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: British government is left reeling after a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after uprising' turns JAR upwards into RAJ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raj was the period of British imperial government in India, hence colonial rule.

clue.text: Their timing is off the cuff?

definitions.text: Their timing is off the cuff?

parts.words: Their timing is off the cuff?
parts.note: off the cuff usually means improvised, but timepieces worn on the arm literally tell the time from just beyond the shirt cuff

explanation.surface: Someone's timing is improvised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the cuff' suggests spontaneity; read literally it places the timepieces at the wrist, by the cuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Watches worn on a strap round the arm sit right next to a sleeve's cuff and give the time.

clue.text: Supporting, loudly, college teacher

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
F, forte, is the musical marking for loudly

explanation.surface: Someone speaks up, loudly, in favour of an academic.
explanation.definitionFit: Short informal form of professor, the senior teaching rank at a college or university.

clue.text: Detained by wet weather on bad run, I collapsed

indicators.note: something collapsed has fallen apart, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Kept in by the rain after a poor run, a runner falls in a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges the nine letters of ON BAD RUN I.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound here means confined, so being stuck indoors because of rain is to be kept in by it.

clue.text: Managed to block football club's money, once

indicators.note: the club letters block the word for managed by surrounding it

parts.note: to run something is to manage it, past tense ran

explanation.surface: Someone contrived to freeze a football club's funds in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the money as former: the franc was replaced by the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc was the currency of France and Belgium before the euro, hence former money.

clue.text: Counting the number of floors out loud? Doing some recounting?

definitions.text: Counting the number of floors out loud?
definitions.meaning: playfully, telling (counting) storeys, the floors of a building, said aloud
recounting means narrating a tale, the second sense here

explanation.surface: Someone counts building levels aloud, then counts again.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a pun: 'telling' also means counting, and storey sounds the same as story.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrating tales is recounting them, so relating stories fits the second reading exactly.

clue.text: Plucky musician with a beam following band endlessly

indicators.note: the beam comes after the trimmed band in the answer, following it
without its end, so the last letter of the word band is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
a joist is a beam supporting a floor or ceiling

explanation.surface: A brave player teams up with a beam that trails behind a band forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucky' looks like 'brave' but means one who plucks strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjoist plays the banjo, whose strings are plucked, so the player is a plucking musician.

clue.text: Country artist with a measuring of intelligence all round

indicators.note: the intelligence measure goes all round the artist, enclosing it

parts.note: IQ, intelligence quotient, is a measure of intelligence
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: A nation's painter is surrounded by intelligence testing.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a Middle Eastern nation whose capital is Baghdad.

clue.text: Girl embraced by Lorenzo ecstatically

indicators.note: the name is held inside the clue words, embraced by them across the gap between words

explanation.surface: A young woman is hugged by Lorenzo with great joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' shows the name sitting inside lorenZO Ecstatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoe is a female given name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Hitler era corrupt, and more materialistic

indicators.note: corrupt letters are spoiled and altered, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Nazi period was rotten and more worldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges HITLERERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthly means worldly rather than spiritual, so its comparative means more worldly.

clue.text: Retreat from act by sponsor

parts.note: a turn is an act or performance on stage
to back someone is to sponsor or fund them

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws from a show staged by a financial backer.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn back is to go back the way one came, the verb sense of withdraw.

clue.text: Audibly criticises Scottish theologian

indicators.note: heard rather than seen, the word for criticises is said out loud

parts.note: to knock something is to criticise it

explanation.surface: A Scottish churchman openly finds fault.
explanation.walkthrough: John Knox was the 16th-century leader of the Scottish Reformation.
explanation.definitionFit: John Knox was a Protestant reformer and theologian who founded Scottish Presbyterianism.

clue.text: Strict, if retiring, resident magistrate

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word if is read backwards

explanation.surface: A magistrate who lives locally is severe, if shy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like 'shy', describing the magistrate, but signals a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means unyielding and resolute, a synonym of strict.

clue.text: Nimble artisan appearing regularly in Spain and Portugal

indicators.note: only letters at regular intervals show up, here every second letter of the two words

explanation.surface: A skilful craftsman turns up now and then on the Iberian peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters: I B E from Nimble, R I A from artisan.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the name of the peninsula shared by those two countries.

clue.text: Day beginning for old Scottish town

parts.note: Thurs is the short form of Thursday

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of old

explanation.surface: A day marks the start of an ancient Scottish settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: THURSO is a town on the far north coast of Scotland, in Caithness.
explanation.definitionFit: Thurso is a real place in the Highland region, the most northerly town on the British mainland.

clue.text: Yacht I'm manoeuvring left? Not true!

indicators.note: moving the letters about as one manoeuvres a boat, so yacht and I'm are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor claims to be steering a yacht to port, and someone scoffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges YACHTIM into MYTHICA; L for left goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mythical exists only in myth or imagination, so it is false or invented.

clue.text: The lad Tuohy upset

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over and scrambled, so Tuohy is rearranged

explanation.surface: The boy Tuohy is unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges TUOHY.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young man, a boy approaching adulthood.

clue.text: Fool having short film wound back

indicators.note: a film wound back runs in reverse, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: vid is the short form of video, a film

explanation.surface: An idiot owns a brief movie that has been rewound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound back' turns VID into DIV. DIV is British slang for a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an idiot or stupid person, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Victor, with Irish trade union, displays artistic taste

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man named Victor, alongside an Irish union, shows a feel for art.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtu is a love of or knowledge of fine art objects, connoisseurship.

clue.text: Initially fed up, joins in finding Japanese volcano

indicators.note: at the start of each word, so the first letter of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone tired of things joins in, discovering a Japanese mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Fuji is Japan's highest peak, a dormant volcano near Tokyo.

clue.text: English girl: a railway representative

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: An English girl is put forward as the spokesperson for a railway company.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an agent sent on a mission, someone who acts on another's behalf.

clue.text: Second home is something bad

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Owning a holiday home is a wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a wrongful act, an evil or immoral deed.

clue.text: Rosemary, perhaps, the female bishop

parts.note: her is the pronoun for the female
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: Rosemary might be the woman who became a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosemary' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, given as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is one example of a culinary plant, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Some impugn a government, returning to combine in opposition?

indicators.note: the run of letters goes back the way it came, read from right to left
only some of the letters of the clue words are taken, a run found inside them

explanation.surface: Some people attack a government, coming back to unite as its opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes PUGNAG from impugn a government; 'returning' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To gang up is to join together against someone, uniting as a hostile group.
